poe.circuit_parallel.explain: In parallel each resistor is its own path, so the total resistance fell from {resistance_before} to {resistance_after} and more current flows.

poe.titration_double.explain: Each cm³ of this alkali carries twice as much hydroxide, so half the volume, {end_point_after}, neutralises the acid. The pH stays low, then jumps at that point.

poe.gas_heated.question: The gas in this sealed flask is at {pressure_before}. It is warmed from {celsius_before} to {celsius_after}, so the Celsius temperature doubles. What happens to the pressure?
poe.gas_heated.explain: Pressure goes with the kelvin temperature, not the Celsius one. {temperature_before} to {temperature_after} is only a small rise, so the pressure rises by the same small fraction.

poe.function_shift.outcome: The turning point moved from x = {before} to x = {after}.
poe.function_shift.explain: Adding 3 inside the bracket means x needs to be 3 less to give the same value, so every point, the turning point too, moves 3 to the left.

poe.electrolysis_brine.question: Concentrated sodium chloride solution is electrolysed with inert electrodes. What forms at the cathode, the negative electrode?
poe.electrolysis_brine.outcome: Hydrogen bubbled off at the cathode, {cathode_gas_after} of it, and no sodium formed ({cathode_mass_after}).
poe.electrolysis_brine.explain: Water gives H+ ions as well as the salt's Na+ ions. Sodium is far more reactive than hydrogen, so H+ ions take the electrons and hydrogen forms; sodium stays in the solution as ions.
sim.rates.drawing: Reacting particles in a box: circles are the reactant and squares the product, with a bar for the product made so far
poe.rates_hotter.question: The same amount of reactant is used again, but warmed from 20 °C to 40 °C. By the end of the reaction, how much product is there compared with the cooler run?
poe.rates_hotter.outcome: Both runs ended with {product_after} of product. The warmer one got there in {time_after} instead of {time_before}.
poe.rates_hotter.explain: Heating makes collisions more frequent and more energetic, so the reaction is faster. The amount of product is set by how much reactant there is, so it ends the same.
